tools.name: time
tools.description: Return the kernel's current UNIX epoch in seconds.

tools.name: getuid
tools.description: Return the uid + gid agentd is running under.

tools.name: dns_resolve
tools.description: Resolve a hostname to an IPv4 address via the kernel resolver.

tools.name: dhcp_info
tools.description: Return the active DHCP lease (ip, gateway, dns_server, lease).

tools.name: dns_cache_stats
tools.description: Return cumulative DNS resolver cache stats.

tools.name: fbinfo
tools.description: Return framebuffer geometry, or {enabled:false} if the kernel is text-mode only.

tools.name: smp_stats
tools.description: Return SMP topology + per-CPU tick counts.

tools.name: shell.exec
tools.description: Fork+exec a command, capturing stdout / stderr. Runs with agentd's privileges (uid 0). The command path must be a valid ELF in the filesystem.

args.description: Argument list passed after argv[0]=cmd. Up to 15 entries.

tools.name: kv.get
tools.description: Read a value from the persistent agent KV store (session 73). Returns {found, value}. Values up to ~4 KiB; longer entries are still on disk but the JSON response caps the value field.

key.description: 1-64 chars, [A-Za-z0-9_.-], no leading dot, no slashes

tools.name: kv.put
tools.description: Write a value to the persistent agent KV store (session 73). Returns {ok}. Backed by AdventFS, survives reboots.

value.description: Up to ~4 KiB; binary blobs should be base64-encoded client-side.

tools.name: kv.del
tools.description: Delete a key from the persistent agent KV store (session 73). Returns {ok, existed}.

tools.name: kv.list
tools.description: List keys in a namespace, optionally filtered by prefix (session 73). Returns {keys: [...]}. Empty array for a non-existent namespace.

prefix.description: Optional. Match keys starting with this string.

tools.name: kv.stat
tools.description: Return the size and existence of a key (session 73). Returns {exists, size}. Use before kv.get to decide whether to fetch the full value.

tools.name: kv.watch
tools.description: Subscribe the calling connection to KV changes (session 76). Returns {watch_id}. Every successful kv.put / kv.del on a key under (namespace, prefix) pushes a notifications/kv/changed line with {namespace, key, op}. Empty / omitted prefix matches every key in the namespace. Event-driven (no polling). Max 16 concurrent watches per daemon; closing the connection drops all owned watches automatically.

namespace.description: 1-31 chars, must match an existing namespace pattern (no validation here, just length)

prefix.description: Optional. Match keys starting with this string; empty = match all in namespace.

tools.name: kv.unwatch
tools.description: Cancel a kv.watch registration (session 76). Returns {ok}. Only the connection that registered the watch may unwatch it. Closing the connection also unwatches.

watch_id.description: ID returned by a prior kv.watch call.

tools.name: shell.exec_sandboxed
tools.description: Like shell.exec, but the spawned process runs under a syscall sandbox AND optional resource caps. Any syscall not in the named policy returns -1 and bumps a per-process denial counter; exceeding a resource cap kills the child with SIGSEGV (RSS) or SIGKILL (CPU / wall-clock). Useful for running untrusted tools without risking the rest of the system. The child and any of its forks inherit both the mask and the caps. The response includes `sandbox_log` (snapshot of /proc/<child_pid>/sandbox) and `limits_state` (snapshot of /proc/<child_pid>/limits) captured just before the child is reaped.

cmd.description: Command to exec under the sandbox.

args.description: Args after argv[0]=cmd. Up to 12 entries (3 are reserved for the sandbox wrapper prefix).

policy.description: Syscall allow-list template. minimal = compute (no I/O); compute = + mmap/munmap; readfs = + read-only filesystem; netclient = + outbound TCP/UDP + DNS.

limits.description: Optional per-task resource caps (session 71). All fields are non-negative integers; 0 or omitted = no cap. Monotonic-tighten: once set, the child cannot loosen them.

max_rss_kb.description: Max heap+mmap resident size, in kilobytes. Overrun on alloc -> -1 / SIGSEGV.

max_cpu_ms.description: Max total CPU time the task may consume, in milliseconds (PIT 10 ms granularity). Overrun -> SIGKILL.

max_fds.description: Max simultaneously-open file descriptors. Overrun -> alloc_fd returns -1.

max_wall_ms.description: Wall-clock deadline relative to setlimit, in milliseconds. Overrun -> SIGKILL.

tools.name: shell.exec_background
tools.description: Spawn a child the same way shell.exec does, but return immediately with {job_id, pid}. The child's stdout/stderr stream into per-job 4 KiB ring buffers; agents pull via shell.job.read OR get pushed bytes via shell.job.subscribe + notifications/job.output. Optional `policy` + `limits` work identically to shell.exec_sandboxed. Up to 8 jobs may be RUNNING at once; older EXIT slots are recycled when the table fills.

tools.name: shell.job.list
tools.description: Enumerate every non-FREE job slot. Returns {jobs:[{job_id,pid,cmd,state,done,exit_code?,stdout_total,stderr_total,policy?},...]}.

tools.name: shell.job.status
tools.description: Detailed status of one job (same shape as one entry in shell.job.list).

tools.name: shell.job.read
tools.description: Pull bytes from a job's stdout/stderr ring buffers. Pass the previous read's `stdout_next` / `stderr_next` as the new offsets to consume incrementally. `stdout_skipped` / `stderr_skipped` count bytes the ring has overwritten (lost) since the requested offset; in that case `stdout` / `stderr` start at the oldest still-retained byte. `done` flips true once the child has been reaped AND both pipes have hit EOF.

stdout_offset.description: Default 0; pass last call's stdout_next to consume new bytes.

max.description: Max bytes per stream this call. Default and ceiling: 2048.

tools.name: shell.job.wait
tools.description: Block until the job exits OR timeout_ms milliseconds pass. Returns {job_id, done, exit_code?, timed_out}. The wait is queued inside agentd; other connections and jobs continue running. Default timeout 5 s, hard cap 300 s.

tools.name: shell.job.cancel
tools.description: Send SIGKILL to a RUNNING job. Returns {job_id, killed}. Does not block — the next event-loop reap promotes the slot to EXIT.

tools.name: shell.job.delete
tools.description: Free an EXIT-state job slot so it can be recycled. Refuses to remove a still-running job (caller must cancel + wait first). Returns {job_id, removed, reason?}.

tools.name: shell.job.subscribe
tools.description: Register the calling connection to receive notifications/job.output (per-chunk stdout/stderr) and notifications/job.exit. Returns the current stdout_total / stderr_total so the agent can pair the push stream with a baseline shell.job.read offset. Subscriptions are per-connection — closing the connection unsubscribes automatically.

tools.name: shell.job.unsubscribe
tools.description: Drop a prior shell.job.subscribe registration on the calling connection.

tools.name: cron.create
tools.description: Submit a scheduled task (session 77). kind=oneshot fires once at fire_at (or now+delay_sec); kind=recurring fires every interval_sec until cancelled or max_runs hit. Optional sandbox policy + per-task resource limits, same shape as shell.exec_sandboxed. Each entry is persisted as /var/cron/<id>.json and survives reboot. Fires spawn a session-74 background job; subscribe via cron.subscribe to get notifications/cron.fired. Returns {entry_id, fire_at}.

fire_at.description: Absolute UNIX epoch; mutually exclusive with delay_sec.

delay_sec.description: Fire at now + delay_sec; mutually exclusive with fire_at.

concurrent.description: If false (default), skip the next fire when the previous run is still RUNNING.

tools.name: cron.list
tools.description: List every cron entry currently in the table (session 77). Optional state filter restricts to one of {scheduled, cancelled, expired}. Returns {entries: [...]} with one summary per slot.

tools.name: cron.get
tools.description: Return the full entry record for one cron id, including spawn config + limits (session 77).

tools.name: cron.cancel
tools.description: Mark a cron entry as CANCELLED — no further fires (session 77). Does NOT kill the most recent fire's job (use shell.job.cancel for that). The entry record stays on disk until cron.delete. Returns {ok, was_scheduled}.

tools.name: cron.delete
tools.description: Free a cron entry's slot + remove its /var/cron/<id>.json file (session 77). Any in-flight job from a prior fire keeps running. Returns {ok, removed: id}.

tools.name: cron.subscribe
tools.description: Register the calling connection to receive notifications/cron.fired for this entry (session 77). Up to 4 conns per entry; closing the connection unsubscribes automatically.

tools.name: cron.unsubscribe
tools.description: Drop the calling connection from a cron entry's subscriber list (session 77).
